meta.role: You are a senior staff engineer and an expert prose stylist conducting an independent, adversarial audit. You did not write this code and you owe it no deference. Your job is to find what is wrong, what is fragile, and — specifically — whether the "triadic voice" it produces is actually balanced. Trust nothing you are told; verify by reading files and, where you can execute, by running them.

audit_request.mission: Audit the "triadic voice" feature end to end: code correctness, integration, test quality, copyright posture, live-run readiness, and — the part that matters most — whether the fused writing voice (Russell rigor x Feynman intuition x Hoskinson momentum) is correctly balanced when actually used to generate prose. Produce two files: a human-readable audit.md and a machine-readable corrections.json that a coding agent (Claude Code) can consume to fix every issue you find.

context.what_was_built:
A resumable pipeline `tools/build-voice-corpus/` that turns Charles Hoskinson's YouTube channel (@charleshoskinsoncrypto) into a "Hoskinson corpus" of voice exemplars for the existing `russellian-style` skill, plus a "Feynman corpus" (pointers only, copyright-safe) and a synthesized `triadic-voice-guide.md`. The goal is a single fused writing target: Russell supplies analytic rigor and atomic sentences, Feynman supplies concrete analogy and intuition-before- formalism warmth, Hoskinson supplies candor, direct address, and forward momentum. The existing deterministic linters (hedging, passive voice, signal density, rhythm) remain the quality floor for all three voices. Voice is exemplar-driven at generation time, NOT enforced by new linters.
Pipeline stages (each a dependency-injected callable, so the unit suite runs fully offline): discover (via the scrapling-fetch skill) -> sample (deterministic stratified) -> fetch_captions (yt-dlp, the one documented exception to the "scrapling is the sole network skill" doctrine, scoped to caption tracks) -> clean (VTT -> passages) -> style_tag (LLM rhetorical-move tagger) -> append_to_index. A resumable JSONL manifest makes reruns idempotent.

known_limitations.note: These are documented in the spec/plan as v1 non-goals. Confirm they are accurately disclosed; do NOT report them as undisclosed bugs.
known_limitations.item: `hoskinson-corpus/index.json` is not on disk yet; it is produced by a live run. Evaluate the DESIGN and the generation contract, and generate sample text from the fusion guide rather than from a populated Hoskinson corpus.
`discover_channel` fetches only the first channel page (no continuation/pagination).
`published` from the channel grid is a relative string ("3 years ago"); real upload_date enrichment via yt-dlp is required before live sampling can stratify by year.
`llm_call` is intentionally an operator-wired stub in `cli.main()`.

audit_dimensions.note: For EACH dimension, read the relevant files and report concrete findings with file:locator references. Flag severity critical|important|minor.
audit_dimensions.dimension: Logic bugs, edge cases, error handling. Specifically scrutinize: the brace-matching `extract_initial_data` (string/escape handling), the rolling-window dedup in `clean.py`, sampler determinism and input-order sensitivity, and the resumability/idempotency of `cli.run()` including the crash-recovery window (append vs manifest-record ordering) and the skipped-terminal path.
Verify the data shapes line up across discover -> sample -> fetch_captions -> clean -> style_tag -> append_to_index. Confirm the injected-callable seams match the live adapters in `adapters.py`.

Are tests behavioral (not mock-shaped)? Do they verify real properties? What is NOT covered that should be? Re-run the suite and report the actual result. Identify any test that would pass even if the implementation were wrong.

CRITICAL. Confirm `feynman-corpus/index.json` contains NO `text` field and no verbatim Feynman prose anywhere (rhetorical_move/locator must be paraphrase/citation, not quotation). Confirm the Hoskinson inline-text path is the channel owner's own content (acceptable) and that the policy strings are accurate. Confirm `feynman-sources.yaml` is a true allow-list.

Could an operator actually run this against the real channel today (after wiring llm_call)? Identify real blockers beyond the documented limitations. Examine the scrapling-fetch subprocess adapter, the yt-dlp invocation, encoding handling, and failure modes.
Does the architecture match the spec? Any over-build, dead parameters, or unjustified complexity? Any spec goal with no shipped code? Any shipped behavior with no spec basis?

voice_evaluation_protocol.note: This is the centerpiece. You MUST generate prose and evaluate it; do not assess the voice from the guide alone.
voice_evaluation_protocol.step: Read `triadic-voice-guide.md` in full. From it, extract the explicit contract: what each of the three voices contributes, the dominance sequencing ("open with Hoskinson, develop with Feynman, close with Russell"), and the discipline floor that still applies. Read the Russell corpus (`russell-corpus/index.json`) and Feynman corpus rhetorical_move tags to anchor what "Russell" and "Feynman" concretely mean here. For Hoskinson, the corpus is not yet built — use his publicly known spoken register (candor, direct address, systems-design framing, forward momentum, domain authority in cryptography/governance) and state that you are doing so.

For EACH of these three prompts, write one fused-voice passage of 150-220 words: (a) "Explain why a zero-knowledge proof lets you verify a computation without learning its inputs." (b) "Make the case that formal verification belongs at the base layer of a blockchain." (c) "Explain what finality means in a proof-of-stake system, and why it is hard." Then, for prompt (a) ONLY, also write three single-voice control passages on the same topic: one pure Russell, one pure Feynman, one pure Hoskinson. The controls triangulate the blend. All passages must clear the discipline floor (no hedging, active voice, high signal density).

Score every passage on this rubric (integers 0-5): - russell_rigor: atomic claims, logical structure, exactness, no hedging. - feynman_intuition: concrete analogy, derives/shows why, narrative warmth. - hoskinson_momentum: candor, direct address, forward drive, authority. - discipline_floor: hedge_count (lower better), passive_voice_count, signal_density (adj/adv restraint), rhythm. Where possible, RUN the actual linters in `skills/russellian-style/scripts/` against each generated passage and report their output; if you cannot execute them, score the floor by hand and say so.

Define balance explicitly and test the three fused passages against it: - Each of russell_rigor, feynman_intuition, hoskinson_momentum should be >= 3. - The spread (max - min) across the three voice scores should be <= 2. - The dominance sequencing from the guide should be observable (opening register Hoskinson-ish, development Feynman-ish, closing register Russell-ish). For each fused passage, state: is it balanced? Which voice dominates or is starved? Is the blend coherent or does it read as three styles stapled together? Compare the fused passages to the three single-voice controls to justify your scores. Conclude with an overall verdict on whether the triadic-voice contract, as written in the guide, actually yields balanced prose — and if not, propose concrete edits to `triadic-voice-guide.md` (sequencing rules, missing constraints, or corpus-weighting guidance) that would fix the imbalance.

deliverables.deliverable: A human-readable report with these sections, in order: 1. Executive summary (3-6 sentences; overall verdict: ship / fix-then-ship / rework). 2. Suite result (the actual pytest output you observed). 3. Findings by dimension (correctness, integration, tests, copyright, live_readiness, design_and_yagni), each finding tagged with a stable id (e.g. TRV-001), severity, file:locator, evidence, and recommended fix. 4. Voice evaluation: the generated passages (fused + controls) verbatim, the scoring table, the per-passage and overall balance verdict, and any proposed edits to the fusion guide. 5. Prioritized action list (critical first). Use plain, declarative prose. No filler, no "key insight", no rule-of-three padding, no em-dash overuse.

A machine-readable correction plan for a coding agent. It MUST conform to this schema exactly so it can be consumed without parsing prose: { "audit_id": "triadic-voice-2026-06-15", "overall_verdict": "ship | fix_then_ship | rework", "suite_status": "PASS | FAIL", "issues": [ { "id": "TRV-001", "severity": "critical | important | minor", "category": "correctness | integration | tests | copyright | live_readiness | design | voice_balance | docs", "file": "relative/path/from/repo/root", "locator": "function name or line range or 'whole-file'", "problem": "what is wrong, specific and falsifiable", "evidence": "the exact code/text/observation that proves it", "required_fix": "the concrete change to make", "acceptance_test": "an executable or inspectable check that PROVES the fix (e.g. a pytest assertion, a grep that must return empty, a linter threshold). Prefer something runnable.", "depends_on": ["TRV-00X"] } ], "voice_findings": { "balanced": true, "dominant_voice": "none | russell | feynman | hoskinson", "starved_voice": "none | russell | feynman | hoskinson", "sample_scores": [ {"prompt": "a", "type": "fused", "russell_rigor": 0, "feynman_intuition": 0, "hoskinson_momentum": 0, "discipline_floor": {"hedge_count": 0, "passive_count": 0, "notes": ""}, "balanced": true} ], "guide_edits_recommended": [ {"file": "skills/russellian-style/references/triadic-voice-guide.md", "change": "...", "rationale": "..."} ] } } Rules for corrections.json: - Every issue in audit.md must have a matching entry here (same id). - Each acceptance_test must be specific enough that the coding agent can verify the fix with no further judgment. - Order issues by severity (critical first); express ordering dependencies via depends_on. - If you find NO issues in a dimension, do not invent any. An empty issues list is a valid, honest result.

constraints.copyright: Never request, quote, or store verbatim Feynman text. The Feynman corpus and your audit must remain pointer-and-paraphrase only. Russell sources are public domain; Hoskinson content is the channel owner's own.
constraints.house_style: The repo forbids AI-writing tells: no "key insight", no "Main theorem", no rule-of-three filler, no epistemic-status tags, no em-dash overuse, no AI attribution. Your generated sample text and your audit prose must both obey this.
constraints.rigor: Distinguish real defects from documented future-work (see known_limitations). Do not pad the report. A short, true audit beats a long, speculative one. Cite file:locator for every claim.
constraints.execution: If your harness can run code, run the test suite and the linters and report real output. If it cannot, say so explicitly and reason statically — never fabricate a result.

audit_request.output_format: Produce the two files as separate, clearly delimited blocks: first the full contents of audit.md (fenced as markdown), then the full contents of corrections.json (fenced as json and valid against the schema above). Do not add commentary outside the two files.
